sentences.text:
The petitioner had approached the learned Special Judge (CBI), Court No.I-cum-Additional Sessions Judge,
Bhubaneswar in BLAPL No.897 of 2024 praying for grant of bail.

entities.text:
Special Judge (CBI), Court No.I-cum-Additional Sessions Judge,
Bhubaneswar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The learned Court below vide its order dated 07.05.2024 rejected the bail application of the petitioner.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement on bail.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner, submits that, except the present bail application, no other bail application of the petitioner is pending in any other Court relating to the aforesaid F.I.R.
3.
The prosecution case as per the F.I.R. is that, on 05.02.2024, the complainants have reported at P.S inter-alia alleging that, they have have invested huge amount on the allurement of the petitioner.
Rasmi Panda paid Rs.18 lakhs and Rs.35 lakhs paid by Ranjan Kumar Panda respectively and an amount of Rs.4 lakhs was deposited inthe Bank Account of the petitioner by the complainant.

So also the payment by the other investors, such as, Rajesh Kumar Panda Rs.18 lakhs, Sudipta Pati Rs.3 lakhs, Rajsekhar Reddy Jangam Rs.1 lakh, Prajakta Sanas Rs.3 kahs, Manisha Sandip Sanas Rs.2 Atmajyoti Nayak vs State Of Odisha .... 1 lakhs and Ashutosh Panda Rs.27 lakhs to the petitioner in his personal account of the State Bank of India, Palaspalli Branch, Bhubaneswar.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
All the money collected by the petitioner on false promises has been siphoned away by the petitioner Hence, the F.I.R.
4.

Mr. Panda, learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from his client, submits that, he would deposit Rs.2 lakhs to show his bonafide and he also undertakes that, after being released on bail, he will make all possible endeavors to make sure to settle the dispute with all depositor/
investor and refund the entire defaulted amount to the investors.
He also submits that, the petitioner can be sent to the mediation as well.
5. Regard being had to the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the learned trial Court is directed to explore the possibility of settlement.

6. In view of the aforementioned submissions and taking into consideration the period of custody of the petitioner i.e. from 15.04.2024 and the nature of accusation and the fact that the petitioner has already refunded about Rs.10 crores to the investors, I am inclined to admit the petitioner on bail.

In the event the petitioner is found to be wanted for violation of any of the bail conditions imposed by this Court or the trial Court even on a single occasion, the prosecution is at liberty to move appropriate application before the Court below for cancellation of the concession of bail granted by this Court.
If such application is filed, the trial Court should decide the application on its own merit.
8. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
(S.S. Mishra) Judge Subhasis Location: High Court of Orissa, Cuttack.
